 Apec summit Apec summit live: Xi and Putin give opening speeches as world leaders gather in China
 Summit in Chinese tech hub Shenzhen set to include highly anticipated meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin
 Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit 
 What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds 
 LIVE  Updated  9m ago Kate Lamb Tue 17 Nov 2026 23.26 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 22.46 EST Share Key events 8m ago Apec explained 
 27m ago Xi Jinping calls for freer trade, greater cooperation on AI 
 49m ago Apec opens in China's tech hub Shenzen 
 Leaders from Apec’s 21 economies are expected to discuss trade and AI at meetings in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: China Pool/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Leaders from Apec’s 21 economies are expected to discuss trade and AI at meetings in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: China Pool/Getty Images Kate Lamb Tue 17 Nov 2026 23.26 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 22.46 EST Share Key events 8m ago Apec explained 
 27m ago Xi Jinping calls for freer trade, greater cooperation on AI 
 49m ago Apec opens in China's tech hub Shenzen 
 8m ago 23.26 EST Apec explained
 What is Apec you ask? 
 Well, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) club has 21 members that represent more than 50% of global GDP and are home to about 2.7 billion people.
 View image in fullscreen Buildings are seen with APEC signs at dusk in Shenzhen, the host city for the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, in China’s southern Guangdong province on November 15, 2026. Photograph: Greg Baker/AFP/Getty Images China, Russia and the US are three of the largest members. Others include Australia, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Singapore, and Vietnam.
 Read below our handy short explainer on how it all started.
 What is Apec - explained in 30 seconds Read more Share 17m ago 23.18 EST Rebecca Bailey The Asia Group’s George Chen is at the CEO summit and sent the Guardian some thoughts on Xi’s speech, which he said was “largely expected”, featuring technology and innovation prominently.
 Xi positioned China as “a force for stability and predictability in an increasingly uncertain world”, he said.
 He added:
 double quotation mark While Xi never mentioned export controls, Nvidia or the United States directly in his speech, the underlying message was unmistakable: China intends to pursue a more open and cooperative approach to technology development. That message is likely to resonate with many countries in the Global South and reinforces Beijing’s effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington.”
 Share 27m ago 23.08 EST Xi Jinping calls for freer trade, greater cooperation on AI
 Rebecca Bailey President Xi Jinping addressed the Apec CEO summit this morning. His speech called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, as well as greater cooperation around artificial intelligence.
 He also emphasised the importance of the World Trade Organization, and said China was expanding its imports of quality goods and services.
 View image in fullscreen President of China Xi Jinping speaks during the 2026 APEC CEO Summit on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: China Pool/Getty Images 
 double quotation mark We should not only eliminate trade and investment barriers... but also promote inclusive and balanced development.
 We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition.”
 Share Updated at  23.25 EST 42m ago 22.53 EST Rebecca Bailey We’re back for day two of the Apec CEO Summit in China’s southern tech hub of Shenzhen . Today the summit will be addressed by APEC leaders, with President Xi Jinping set to give a keynote speech .
 Bilateral meetings will continue on the sidelines, although the most eye-catching – Xi and Donald Trump , and the US-China-Russia trilateral – won’t be until Thursday. Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen this morning, greeted by a red carpet, soldiers and pom pom-waving dancers dressed in fuchsia and blue. Communist party politburo member Cai Qi , often described as Xi’s right-hand man, was there to meet him.
 View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin arrives in Shenzhen ahead of Apec. Photograph: Anupam Nath/AFP/Getty Images Trump will leave Manila, where he has been attending the Asean forum, later on Wednesday. The Associated Press reports that he has expressed excitement about his own welcome ceremony: “I hear we’re going to have quite a landing,” he told reporters. “It’s going to be a beautiful thing.”
 Aside from the high-level hobnobbing, delegates are “working around the clock” to agree on a joint statement for Thursday, a senior Apec official told Reuters on Tuesday.
 Carlos Kuriyama, director of the Apec policy support unit, said all 21 Apec members agreed on the need to ensure trade is “not only open, but also fair”.
 He said they were also discussing the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence .
 double quotation mark They are working very hard to make sure that we can have a common language.”
 Share 49m ago 22.46 EST Apec opens in China's tech hub Shenzen
 It’s been a big week already for diplomatic summits , with the most anticipated among them, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leader’s meeting, starting today in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzen.
 Some observers have noted that we could be about to witness a Yalta 2.0 , a reference to a major 1945 wartime conference attended by Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.
 That’s because the leaders of the US, China and Russia – namely Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin – will meet for trilateral talks at the summit to discuss the wars in Iran and Ukraine, denuclearisation, economics, tech and trade.
 View image in fullscreen Xi Jinping and leaders pose for a group photo at the start of the Apec summit. Photograph: Pedro Pardo/EPA Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting North Korea’s Kim Jong-un in what would be their first meeting of his second term.
 Here is a quick recap of the latest before the event kicks off:
 China’s foreign ministry said the leaders “will exchange views in-depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance”. The ministry added that: “Stronger communication among China , Russia and the United States, along ​with managing differences and stabilising relations, serves the interests of all three countries.”
 The Kremlin said: “The significance and symbolism of this meeting are hard to overestimate. ” But it has dismissed comparisons with the 1945 Yalta meeting saying they were just “games of political scientists”.
 In a call this week, China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, and the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio , “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearisation”, the US state department said.
